new_findings.finding: D437-R1 (4)'s qualifier "문서에 0회 등장" (the 4th mechanism appears 0 times in the docs) is literally false, and the false version changes the methodological lesson. The runtime spawn-wrapper mechanism WAS documented on 2026-07-11 with the very same schemas.py:488 citation D437-R1 uses: session_20260711_d332_verification_briefing_d333_prechecks.md:27-31 reads "코드 라인: d330 probe `:482` `_try_make_sensor`(post-PLAY 수동 생성), d332 probe `:504` zero-reporter spawn / `:643` sensor contract / `:705` mirror recook 실재. `activate_contact_sensors(prim_path, threshold=0.0)` 시그니처 확인 (installed isaaclab `schemas.py:488`)". A second doc, session_20260711_grasp_g0a_d332_static_collision_discriminator.md:115-117, cites the same code region ("d332 probe:504-559") as "one cylinder-owned, scene-registered pre-PLAY sensor with an explicit `0.0N` reporter threshold". Neither July doc is referenced anywhere in the current START_HERE.md (grep for 20260710/20260711 -> 0 hits). So the true failure is not "the project never wrote this down" but "the project wrote it down in July and then dropped it out of the boot reading set", which is a knowledge-retention/reading-set failure rather than a documentation-authoring failure, and points at a different remedy.

new_findings.finding: What the d332/d362 evidence actually licenses, stated precisely. The working instrumentation in d332/d333/d362 is ENTIRELY OBJECT-SIDE and never touches the robot: (a) the runtime call at d332:519 applies the reporter to `prim` returned by the cylinder spawner — the Sponge/cylinder prim — not to the robot; (b) the ContactSensor at d332:558 / d362:1189 is mounted on prim_path '/World/envs/env_.*/Sponge', with the robot links appearing only as filter_prim_paths_expr entries. Meanwhile roarm_stack_env.py:150 governs '/World/envs/env_.*/Robot'. Therefore the two are configuring DISJOINT prims, and the licensed inference is exactly: 'a False robot-side activate_contact_sensors does not block object-side contact reporting.' It does NOT license: (i) any statement about whether a True robot-side flag would have produced data in the 43rd; (ii) any transfer of d362's contact behavior to the 43rd's env/object/scene; (iii) any claim that the runtime-override mechanism is what made d362 succeed as opposed to the ContactSensor registration — the two were never varied independently in any cited run.

new_findings.finding: N-1's '0.7483 x (1 - 0.174663) = 0.6176' is an algebraic identity, not a reproduction. The sentence as compressed into DECISIONS.md cannot fail and therefore carries zero evidential weight for 'a mechanical-resistance signature'. Attacked all 13 checks and all 6 new_findings; independently recomputed every numeric claim from primary files. Result: 11 SURVIVES, 3 REFUTED, 2 WEAKENED, 0 INCONCLUSIVE.

The re-derivation's citation work is very good — I could not break a single file:line citation against d330, d328, d332, d333, d362, t3t_grasp_stdout.log, the 48th/49th docs, or the D436-R3/R4 ranges. The two July 2026 counterexample documents are real, on point, and verbatim at the cited lines, and I independently confirmed the narrow-scope half too (d332 appears 0 times across all four pre-panel documents).

Three things break.

(1) REFUTED — the report's central downgrade of D437-R1 (4)'s causal clause. The auditor concluded that '등록 0건이라 전 측정 0' is unsupported and that the zero is 'over-determined by at least two sufficient causes'. It never opened the artifact holding the per-step contact rows. d328's RRD trace records verbatim `'contact_force': {'available': False, 'error': 'AttributeError("'ContactSensor' object has no attribute '_timestamp'")'}` — present in all three d328 RRDs. `_timestamp` is created only inside SensorBase._initialize_impl, reached only via the PLAY-timeline callback that scene registration supplies. Non-registration IS the operative cause. Three corollaries: the summary's max_contact_force_n = 0.0 is a default fill (d328:148 `.get('max_force_n', 0.0)`, :162 fallback), so endorsing 'the zero VALUES are confirmed' is a generation-vs-measurement confusion; first_contact_force_step = -1 is quoted without its `v > 1.0` N convention (d328:163) while the d330 field placed beside it uses `> 1.0e-6` (d330:603); and 'BOTH stages' is the wrong denominator — there are three (.step1_cube_removed, .cube_present_evidence, .final_retest).

(2) REFUTED — MINOR #3's 'sharp contrast' between d328's ok=True and d330's 4/4 ok=false is a convention mismatch of the C-8 family. d328:96 returns ok=True straight after the constructor with no initialisation attempt; d330:510 returns ok=false only after an explicit `sensor._initialize_impl()` at :498. Two different code paths, compared as if one boolean.

(3) REFUTED — check 'A (extra)' / the corroboration INFO finding. d330's gate has no contact-force criterion at all: .gate.failure_counts = {contact_height:4, fixed_jaw_gap:3, fixed_jaw_penetration:0, jaw_tangent:0, object_displacement:10, tcp_pose:8}, so verdict=FAIL and pass_all_count=0/10 (denominator: all 10 gate rows) are off-criterion and would have made the 'failure precedent' reading more arguable, not 'unarguable'. The remaining two items (argmax_body_name='' and the two empty maps) are not independent evidence — d330:588-595 initialises all five contact fields together and they are overwritten only from row['contact_force'], which is {'available': False} whenever the sensors are None. One datum restated five times.

Also REFUTED as an untraceable number: the MAJOR finding's evidence field states `grep -nE '20260710|20260711|d332|d333' START_HERE.md -> only :26 and :261`. Working tree returns 56, 120, 309; committed HEAD returns 0 hits and is only 245 lines long, so :261 cannot exist there; and working-tree lines 24-28 / 259-263 contain none of the four terms. The conclusion is undamaged (the 20260710/20260711 sub-pattern is 0 hits in both versions), but the quoted result matches nothing — and working-tree :56/:120/:309 in fact carry the d332 :503-524 mechanism into the current dashboard.

WEAKENED: the MAJOR finding's reframing to 'knowledge-retention rather than documentation-authoring failure, pointing at a different remedy' is scope-dependent, and the auditor's own check D concedes the narrow reading holds; MAJOR severity overstates it. And INFO (a)'s d362 ':1190 not :1191' is a mild reverse false accusation — 49th:155 cites the range 1178-1191, which contains 1190, so there is no off-by-one in the record.

The report's best surviving work: the 2/3 precedent recount with d332 as the missing third (all twelve line citations across d362/d333/d332/d328 verified exact), MINOR #2 (49th:138 and D436-R4:26810 verbatim — action known, precedent unrecognised), and the d330 lifecycle INFO finding, which is internally inconsistent with the auditor's own MINOR #3 since it correctly diagnoses for d330 the same defect it argued away for d328.

Consequently 'the d332 path yields contact data' does NOT need scoping to closure — it is true in the baseline window too; only the robot-link subset needs scoping.

VERDICT: the re-derivation is arithmetically excellent but its headline judgement is wrong, and its one UNVERIFIABLE was premature.

WHAT HELD (I attacked and failed to break): every line-number, hash, size, field-path, and count in checks[0]-[16] reproduces from the primary files. I independently re-read all cited lines in roarm_stack_env.py, d332, d333, d351, d362, roarm_cube_push_env.py, roarm_rl/__init__.py, the t3t frozen script/log/results/CSV, and the isaaclab source; re-hashed d362_worker_summary.json (10f7bd39...b217d / 96,598 B), g0a_d333 summary (17f8dc23... / 16,301 B), and both attempt3 USD layers (a4be58e8... / 043a5d35...); and decoded both .pyc headers (flags=0, srcmtime 1778951575, srcsize 70559 — exact match). The strongest surviving contributions are (a) the disjoint-prim structural observation (object-side reporter/sensor vs robot-side :150) and (b) the 43rd's self-contained absence proof (0 ContactSensor / 0 flag / 324 leaves with 0 contact / 24 CSV cols with 0 contact / LIFT_FAIL).

WHAT BROKE — three findings, in descending severity:

1. new_findings[0] REFUTED, and this is the report's headline. The auditor asserts no run exists pairing activate_contact_sensors=True with absent contact data, so D437-R1's "neither necessary nor sufficient" is only half-licensed. sim_scripts/cyl34_top_view_d330_grasp_g0a_alignment_probe.py:331 sets exactly that field to True on the same RoArmCubeTap10cmEnvCfg lineage, registers robot-side ContactSensors (d330:486,:494), and gets 4/4 "Failed to initialize contact reporter", robot_net_max_force_n=0.0, robot_net_first_contact_step=-1 over trace_steps=320. Worse: D437-R1 CITES that run by name, byte-size and hash four paragraphs below the sentence the auditor quoted (DECISIONS.md:26967-26970 vs :26953). The NOT-NECESSARY leg is [MEASURED], not [INFERRED]. Recommended wording change to D437-R1 should be rejected.

2. checks[17] UNVERIFIABLE REFUTED. pxr is reachable read-only with zero installs via the already-present isaacsim extscache (PYTHONPATH + LD_LIBRARY_PATH) — a path the repo's own d330 artifact records as its resolved pxr.Usd. In that same 200-step window the same sensor read support_table_fz_last50_median_n = 7.0636 N, gated by the preregistered check support_table_fz_last50_median_gt_1n=true; the robot-link -1s are the experiment's designed negative control (robot_filter_max_n all 0.0, precommand_robot_contact_confound=false).

THE SECOND ERROR. "Exactly one ±1 fork" collapses to at least five, including two the record documents explicitly and two that live only in immutable git history the auditor never opened: a four-way 31/32/33/34 fork at the 37th resolved by fiat (38th doc:39-40); MEMORY 35 vs doc 38 at the 38th; a THREE-way 40/41/42 fork at the 40th resolved by the USER'S BOOT PROMPT — a source outside the repo entirely (git 420e2f4:START_HERE.md:181-182), which is the actual reason the absolute base is unrecoverable; a 43→42→43 flip-flop inside the 41st recorded in commit subjects d24e3b3 and 420e2f4; and a committed 43rd intermediate of 46 with one refusal @234% (ae218d2:165) versus the final 47 with two. THE THIRD ERROR is the most instructive for this axis. - **Deeper closing bought tipping, not lift.** Leg 3 is the deepest rung (17.00°, 8.456648 mm commanded interference) and produced the largest tilt (`tilt_deg` max 3.3237° within lift). Its apparent "best object rise" of +0.0330 mm is entirely that tip — `(H/2)cos t + R sin t = 0.025799 m` reproduces the logged centre height to 0.0004 mm — and the tilt-corrected lift-off is 0.0078 mm against a 6.000 mm gate. This is direct evidence against **(d)** as a standalone remedy and is consistent with the standing note that **(1)** worsens tip-over.
- **The grip signature starts later and is weaker than the published anchor pair implies.** The low anchor (19.50°, r = 0.180591) sits *inside* the zero-interference band [0.180558, 0.180673]; the first genuine departure is the 19.00° rung at 3.797844 mm commanded interference. So the kinematic evidence that harder closing produces measurable resistance is thinner than N-1's headline suggests — again pressure against **(d)**.

Neither result promotes **(1)** over **(2)** or vice versa. The friction one-line fragility (`roarm_stack_env.py:118`, effective 0.40/0.30 vs a counterfactual 0.70/0.65 under 'average') applies identically to all three options and is therefore ranking-neutral.

**Nothing here authorizes proceeding.** The one thing that *would* move the ranking — an actual contact-force measurement during closure — still does not exist, and producing it is exactly path (e).
